# sendgrid_template_version (Resource)

Manages a single version of a SendGrid transactional template. Only one version of a template can be `active` (served when sending mail with that template) at a time; setting `active = true` on one version does not automatically deactivate others in Terraform state, matching the API's own behavior.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sendgrid_template_version" "welcome_email_v1" {
  template_id  = sendgrid_template.welcome_email.id
  name         = "v1"
  subject      = "Welcome, {{name}}!"
  html_content = "<p>Welcome, {{name}}!</p>"
  active       = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of this template version.
- `subject` (String) The subject of this template version.
- `template_id` (String) The ID of the template this version belongs to.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether this is the active version served for the template.
- `editor` (String) The editor used in the SendGrid UI for this version: `code` or `design`.
- `generate_plain_content` (Boolean) If true, `plain_content` is always regenerated from `html_content`.
- `html_content` (String) The HTML content of this version. Maximum of 1,048,576 bytes.
- `plain_content` (String) The plain-text content of this version. Generated from `html_content` unless `generate_plain_content` is `false`.
- `test_data` (String) For dynamic templates only: mock JSON data used for template preview and test sends.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The template version's UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) The time this template version was last updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sendgrid_template_version.welcome_email_v1 <template_id>/<version_id>
```
